zh.headline: OpenAI 应美国政府要求，将分阶段发布 GPT-5.6
zh.observation: 今天最值得关注的信号是 AI 安全监管进入实操阶段——美国政府直接要求 OpenAI 分阶段发布 GPT-5.6，这意味着模型发布节奏将从"越快越好"转向"可控有序"。与此同时，推理成本正在成为行业分水岭：GLM-5.2 以五分之一的成本匹敌 Opus 4.7，而 OpenAI 自研芯片 Jalapeño 的发布也表明头部玩家正在用硬件手段锁定成本优势。最后，Agent 工程化正在从"烧 Token 堆功能"转向"算 ROI"，Claude Code 团队的反思和 Patronus AI 的 5000 万美元融资都指向同一个方向——Agent 的下一波竞争不在于能力上限，而在于可靠性、成本和可测试性。

en.headline: OpenAI to Stagger Release of GPT-5.6 at U.S. Government Request
en.observation: The most significant signal today is AI safety regulation entering an operational phase—the U.S. government directly asking OpenAI to stagger GPT-5.6's release means model release cadence is shifting from "faster is better" to "controlled and orderly." Meanwhile, inference cost is becoming an industry dividing line: GLM-5.2 matches Opus 4.7 at one-fifth the cost, while OpenAI's in-house Jalapeño chip signals top players are locking in cost advantages through hardware. Finally, agent engineering is moving from "burn tokens, stack features" to "calculate ROI"—Claude Code team's reflections and Patronus AI's $50M funding both point to the same direction: the next wave of agent competition won't be about capability ceiling, but about reliability, cost, and testability.
